coreLogic: BusinessHours::addWorkingHours in include/class.businesshours.php (delegated via BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours in include/class.schedule.php)
consumers: Ticket::getSLADueDate in include/class.ticket.php (sole direct call site at line 557; receives mutated DateTime, resets timezone to DB timezone, returns formatted 'Y-m-d H:i:s' string or null)
Ticket::updateEstDueDate in include/class.ticket.php (calls getSLADueDate(true) and assigns result to $this->est_duedate, then Ticket::save() persists to database)
Ticket::getEstDueDate in include/class.ticket.php (returns getDueDate() ?: getSLADueDate() for display/comparison)
Ticket::clearOverdue in include/class.ticket.php (calls getSLADueDate() and nulls $this->est_duedate when SLA due datetime is in the past)
Ticket::checkOverdue in include/class.ticket.php (static cron query selects open tickets where est_duedate < NOW() and calls markOverdue(); est_duedate populated via updateEstDueDate chain)
inputShape: Datetime $date (object passed by value but mutated in place); optional BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null; optional array &$timeline = [] passed by reference for audit log population on successful business-hours path
outputShape: Always returns the same DateTime object reference passed as $date, mutated in place (never allocates a new DateTime). When business-hours schedule path succeeds, &$timeline is populated with string audit entries from BusinessHours::getTimeline(). When no schedule resolves or schedule addWorkingHours returns false, falls back to wall-clock DateInterval addition on the same object.
sideEffects: Reads global $cfg in SLA::addGracePeriod for OsticketConfig::getDefaultSchedule() fallback when neither argument schedule nor SLA schedule resolves
SLA::getSchedule() lazy-loads BusinessHoursSchedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getScheduleId()) database SELECT on first access, caching result on SLA::$_schedule instance property
OsticketConfig::getDefaultSchedule() may lazy-load BusinessHoursSchedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getDefaultScheduleId()) database SELECT, caching on Config::$defaultSchedule
BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup() delegates to Schedule::lookup() / parent::lookup() database SELECT filtered by FLAG_BIZHRS
Mutates input DateTime $date in place in both code paths: schedule path via downstream addWorkingHours, fallback path via $date->add(DateInterval) with round(grace_period * 3600) seconds
Populates caller &$timeline array by reference when schedule path succeeds: BusinessHoursSchedule assigns $timeline = $bhrs->getTimeline() after BusinessHours::addWorkingHours returns truthy
BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours constructs ephemeral BusinessHours($this) instance (no persistence)

BusinessHours::addWorkingHours reads Schedule::getNumEntries() which calls Schedule::getEntries() triggering ScheduleEntry::objects()->filter(['schedule_id' => ...]) database SELECT if entries not cached on schedule
BusinessHours::addWorkingHours calls DateTime::setTimezone($this->getSchedule()->getDatetimeZone()) mutating input DateTime timezone to schedule timezone
Schedule::getDatetimeZone() calls Schedule::getTimezone() which reads global $cfg via $cfg->getTimezone() when schedule timezone field is unset
BusinessHours::initOccurrences resets BusinessHours instance $this->workhours and $this->holidays arrays to empty on each invocation inside the while loop
BusinessHours::initOccurrences calls $this->getSchedule()->getEntries() and ScheduleEntry::getOccurrences() to populate workhours occurrence map (database reads if entries uncached)

BusinessHours::initOccurrences calls $this->getSchedule()->getHolidaysSchedules() which lazy-loads each HolidaysSchedule via HolidaysSchedule::lookup($id) database SELECT, caching array on BusinessHoursSchedule::$holidays

Schedule::getHolidays() reads schedule configuration JSON via Schedule::getConfiguration() -> Schedule::getConfig() -> new Config('schedule.'.$id)->getInfo() database read for holiday schedule id list
Holiday schedule entries loaded via HolidaysSchedule::getEntries() ScheduleEntry database SELECT for each linked holiday schedule
BusinessHours::addWorkingHours appends audit strings to BusinessHours::$timeline instance property via private timeline() method throughout partial-day, holiday-skip, apply, and backtrack steps

BusinessHours::addWorkingHours mutates input DateTime in place via DateTime::modify() advancing to end of business day or holiday end, and DateTime::sub(DateInterval) for backtrack when accumulated seconds exceed requested hours
Partial-day branch: when occurrence date equals $date date and not after-hours and not before-hours, sets $partial=true and uses ScheduleEntry::diffTime($date) instead of full ScheduleEntry::diff()
After-hours branch: when occurrence date equals $date date and ScheduleEntry::isAfterHours($date), continues to next working day without adding time

Holiday branch: when $this->holidays[$d] set, moves $date to holiday end time via modify, skips full-day holidays with continue, sets partial=true and computes $leadtime for partial holidays spanning after business-day start
Backtrack branch: when $_seconds > $seconds after adding day time, subtracts round($_seconds - $seconds) seconds via DateInterval and breaks foreach loop
When grace_period hours is zero or non-numeric, BusinessHours::addWorkingHours returns $date immediately without adding time (truthy, so addGracePeriod returns without wall-clock fallback)
When schedule has zero entries, BusinessHours::addWorkingHours returns false causing BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours to return false and addGracePeriod to fall through to wall-clock fallback
No database writes anywhere in SLA::addGracePeriod, BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours, or BusinessHours::addWorkingHours call chain
constraints: Schedule resolution precedence in addGracePeriod: caller-provided BusinessHoursSchedule argument, then SLA::getSchedule(), then global $cfg->getDefaultSchedule()
Grace period magnitude read from SLA model grace_period field via getGracePeriod() in hours
Ticket::getSLADueDate passes department schedule from $this->getDept()->getSchedule() as explicit schedule argument (Dept lazy-loads via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup before addGracePeriod call)
Ticket::getSLADueDate seeds DateTime from reopen date if set else create date, in cfg DB timezone, before calling addGracePeriod
Ticket::getSLADueDate calls $dt->setTimezone($cfg->getDbTimezone()) after addGracePeriod returns before formatting
addGracePeriod does not call BusinessHours::addWorkingHours directly; only via $schedule->addWorkingHours() on resolved BusinessHoursSchedule
If resolved schedule exists but addWorkingHours returns false (empty schedule entries), addGracePeriod falls through to wall-clock grace addition rather than returning early
Wall-clock fallback uses round(grace_period * 3600) whole seconds, not business-hours arithmetic
Input DateTime is always mutated in place; callers must not assume immutability or a new object reference
$timeline audit log populated only when schedule business-hours path succeeds; not populated on wall-clock fallback path
BusinessHours::initOccurrences uses fixed 72-hour grace_period_hrs window to bound occurrence scanning independent of SLA grace period hours argument

Overdue detection consumes persisted est_duedate (derived from addGracePeriod output) not addGracePeriod directly: Ticket::checkOverdue SQL filter on est_duedate__lt NOW(), Ticket::clearOverdue compares getSLADueDate() to current time
